title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
author: Yaru Niu, Binghong Chen, Changwei Yao, Shangtao Li et al.
description: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. summary: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations.
takeaways: EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations.
A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and proprioceptive states, encouraging the shared trunk to model each embodiment's dynamics.

Across 13 task-embodiment pairs spanning five tasks and six robot embodiments, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid, cross-embodiment pretraining raises MXT+'s average normalized task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 over training from scratch.
